page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading resource contention. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core and memory operations, alongside notable weaknesses in single-core and specialized execution. The instance achieves average results in stress-ng single-core (1812.89) and multi-core (14472.4) tests, as well as an average Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 563.91 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 87.42 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 6205.54. Cryptographic performance is also limited, with the Passmark CPU encryption test falling into the bottom 25% at 1300.22, despite hardware AES support.

This server is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and database operations, where it demonstrates average throughput. For example, static web serving throughput reaches 10.09 GB/sec, and the Geekbench clang compilation score is 9005.0. Conversely, the instance is poorly suited for natural language processing and machine learning tasks; LLM inference text generation for a small 135M model is poor, registering in the bottom 10% at 32.29 tokens/sec. The lack of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators further limits its applicability for high-speed local caching or GPU-intensive workloads. Qualitatively, the ARM-based architecture provides a cost-efficient resource density for multi-threaded applications that do not rely on x86-specific instruction sets.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based general-purpose server featuring 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for multi-core processing, software compilation, and static web serving, with a static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and cryptographic execution are weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a weak Passmark encryption result. Additionally, LLM inference speeds are poor, making it unsuitable for AI workloads. This instance is best utilized for scale-out multi-threaded workloads, static web hosting, and basic database operations where ARM architecture compatibility is met.
